title: Add verified workspace file reading Skill
goal: Expose the existing bounded, secret-filtered Workspace Read operation as a real Skill that reads permitted workspace text files and verifies the returned content.
context: WorkspaceReadTool already implements a safe read operation with path validation, readable-text restrictions, protected-path filtering, secret detection, and a verified result. The Skill runtime currently has an allowlisted workspace.search adapter but no workspace.read-file adapter or default manifest, so Agents cannot request a file's contents through the Skill boundary. The module-backed verifier currently checks only the outer JSON string map; read-file needs to verify the nested tool result and its byte count before claiming success.
forbidden_changes: Do not broaden workspace read/write roots, protected-file rules, readable extensions, or secret filtering.
Do not allow Skill.md to select arbitrary executable code or module IDs outside the existing allowlist.
Do not migrate or overwrite user-edited Agent manifests; migrate only exact prior built-in versions.
Do not bypass policy, Agent scope, module schema checks, cancellation, or output verification.
Do not change unrelated UI, provider, storage, or terminal behavior.
acceptance_criteria: FileSkillStore installs workspace.read-file bound only to tool.workspace.read and the allowlisted workspace.read-file adapter.
The default Agent includes workspace.read-file, while migration updates only exact previous built-in scopes and preserves user-edited manifests.
Vietnamese and English read requests extract one bounded workspace-relative path and return the actual file content through ModuleRuntime.
The read-file verifier requires the nested tool operation, verified flag, workspace-relative path, string content, and accurate UTF-8 byte count.
When workspace tools are disabled, workspace.read-file, workspace.search, and workspace.create-file are excluded from canonical chat/team Agent scopes.
End-to-end tests prove real content readback and fail-closed behavior for secret-like/protected paths and disabled scope.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
A direct WorkspaceReadTool regression proves symlinks cannot escape the workspace root.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
Run the WorkspaceReadTool symlink-escape regression on macOS CI.
recovery: If a regression fails, inspect only the read-file Skill manifest, path adapter, nested output verification, Agent migration, and workspace toggle scope. Preserve the existing WorkspaceReadTool safety checks and rerun all required gates.
